classes.name: Oral atypical antipsychotics
classes.description: Second-generation oral antipsychotics: aripiprazole, quetiapine IR/ER, olanzapine, risperidone, ziprasidone, lurasidone (Latuda), paliperidone ER, cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, iloperidone, clozapine, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or add-on treatment for depression.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.description: Long-acting injectables: aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera), risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo), olanzapine pamoate (Zyprexa Relprevv), haloperidol and fluphenazine decanoate.
classes.plainDescription: A shot every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill.

preferredAgent.sig: Schizophrenia: 10-15 mg once daily. Bipolar mania: 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg/day for both. Add-on for depression: start 2-5 mg once daily, max 15 mg/day. Dose per indication (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill once a day; the dose depends on what it is treating.

records.verificationNote: Read on PDF pp.46-48 (ANTIPSYCHOTICS - MISC., QUINOLINONE, BENZISOXAZOLE, DIBENZAPINES). Every oral atypical on the list is PA-flagged, so the pick is quetiapine IR 25 mg (common generic, labeled for adjunct MDD) as the lowest-barrier product a prescriber would write; PA criteria are not in this document. Absent from the list: Caplyta (lumateperone), Latuda brand, Lybalvi, iloperidone (Fanapt), generic cariprazine, Secuado and Nuplazid (not in class). Olanzapine-fluoxetine capsule is a combination product and was excluded. The document does not say the list is complete, so absent drugs are not coded as excluded. Sig is label dosing, not printed.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL 30 per 30 days; Tier 4 (page 36)
criteria: Schizophrenia: diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone.
Bipolar I or II (bipolar depression): diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to quetiapine AND at least one of: olanzapine or lurasidone.
Major depressive disorder: diagnosis AND prior antidepressant monotherapy AND prior generic atypical antipsychotic as add-on; Caplyta used as adjunct to an antidepressant, not monotherapy.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL 30 per 30 days; Tier 4 (page 38)
criteria: Schizophrenia (age 13+): diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone.
Bipolar I manic or mixed episode (age 10+): prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, or aripiprazole.
Bipolar I depression: diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to quetiapine or lurasidone.
Major depressive disorder: DSM-5 diagnosis AND prior adequate-dose (8+ weeks) antidepressant monotherapy AND prior generic oral atypical antipsychotic as add-on; Vraylar used adjunctively.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL 30 per 30 days; Tier 5 (page 38)
criteria: Major depressive disorder: clinical diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to one generic oral atypical antipsychotic; used as add-on to an antidepressant, not monotherapy.
Schizophrenia: clinical diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to one generic oral atypical antipsychotic.
Agitation with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease: clinical diagnosis AND Rexulti not used as an as-needed (prn) treatment for agitation.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL 30 per 30 days; Tier 5 (page 37)
criteria: Excluded: current opioid use or an episode of acute opioid withdrawal.

Schizophrenia: diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least one generic atypical antipsychotic (olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone).

Bipolar I (acute manic or mixed; maintenance monotherapy): diagnosis AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least one of: olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, ziprasidone, or aripiprazole.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL; Tier 4 (page 36)
criteria: Schizophrenia: used for schizophrenia AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone.
Bipolar I (manic or mixed episode): used for bipolar I AND prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, or aripiprazole.
Titration packs A, B, and C carry the same criteria as the tablet in the criteria document.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL; Tier 5 for tablet, Tier 4 for packs (pages 35-36)
criteria: Schizophrenia: diagnosis AND tried or cannot use at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone.
Bipolar I (manic or mixed episodes): diagnosis AND tried or cannot use at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, or aripiprazole.
Titration packs A, B, and C carry the same criteria as the tablet in the criteria document.

Prior therapy, intolerance, or contraindication to at least 2 of: risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, or lurasidone.

paRequired.reason: PA and QL; Tier 5 (page 37)

MDD (age 18+): diagnosis AND tried or cannot use generic aripiprazole with an antidepressant; Opipza used as add-on to antidepressant, not monotherapy.
